payload.name: Extract Explicitly Stated Personal Values
payload.description: When a user explicitly says something is important to them, matters to them, or that they value it (e.g., 'X is important to me', 'I value X', 'X matters to me'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states a personal value or importance, create a separate durable preference or state candidate preserving that value in the user's own words, even if it is given as the reason for an activity.
If multiple distinct values are stated in one message, capture each value explicitly rather than absorbing them only into an event/activity memory.
During CRUD, when merging such a value into an existing memory, retain the explicit importance wording; do not replace it with only a description of the related activity.
Stop after capturing the stated values; do not infer additional values not explicitly mentioned.

solves: Extraction candidates often paraphrase a user's explicit statement of personal importance into an activity description, dropping the value itself (e.g., keeping the activity but losing that something is important to the user). This skill ensures explicitly stated values and importance are preserved as durable preference/state memories, so later questions asking why the user does something can be answered.
